Christmas markets, lights and an ice rink in the capital.
Vianden's hilltop castle above a snow-covered valley and the town's slate roofs.
Crisp fried potato pancakes with onions, sold at fairs and Christmas markets.

countries.name: Germany
countries.intro: Fairy-tale castles, the best Christmas markets in the world, beer halls and wine valleys, the Bavarian Alps, unrestricted autobahns and creative, gritty Berlin.

sp.text: Spargelzeit white-asparagus season (Apr–June 24), beer gardens reopen, cherry blossom in Bonn (April), Walpurgis Night in the Harz (Apr 30), Frühlingsfest in Munich and Stuttgart.

su.text: Beer gardens and lake swims, Rhine in Flames fireworks, Kieler Woche (June), open-air everything. Long light evenings.

fa.text: Oktoberfest (mid-Sept–early Oct), wine festivals on the Rhine and Mosel, Black Forest foliage, Berlin Festival of Lights, St Martin's lantern parades (Nov 11).

wi.text: 2,500+ Christmas markets (late Nov–Dec 23), skiing in Garmisch and the Allgäu, Carnival in Cologne, Mainz and Düsseldorf (Feb 4–9, 2027).

items.d: Sprawling, edgy capital of history, art, clubs and street food, still marked by the Wall.
Neoclassical gate that became the symbol of reunification.
Walk up Norman Foster's glass dome above the parliament chamber.
1.3 km of the Berlin Wall painted by artists, including the famous Brezhnev–Honecker kiss.
The only preserved section of the death strip, at Bernauer Strasse.

items.n: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
items.k: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
items.d: 2,711 concrete stelae with an underground information centre.

items.w: Pergamon Museum mostly closed for renovation into 2027
items.d: Five museums including the Neues Museum's bust of Nefertiti.
A free outdoor and indoor documentation centre on the site of the Gestapo and SS headquarters, beside a surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall.
A hands-on museum of everyday life in East Germany: sit in a Trabant, open drawers in a recreated tower-block flat and see Stasi bugging gear.
The former headquarters of East Germany's secret police, with Erich Mielke's office preserved and exhibits on surveillance and informants.
The famous Allied crossing point between East and West Berlin. Touristy, but the nearby museum and outdoor panels tell the story of escapes.
Disused airport runway turned park for kites, bikes and barbecues.
Techno at Berghain, Tresor or Sisyphos. Door policies are strict.
Berlin's two street-food icons: sliced sausage with curry ketchup, and the döner kebab, invented by Turkish immigrants in Berlin.
Multicultural neighbourhoods with canal-side bars and markets.
Frederick the Great's Sanssouci Palace and Rococo parks.
Bavarian capital of beer halls, Baroque churches, BMW and the Alps on the horizon.
The world's most famous beer hall, with oompah bands and litre steins.
Munich locals' favourite brewery, serving beer from wooden barrels at the Augustiner-Keller beer garden and the Augustiner Bräustuben.
Chinesischer Turm, Hirschgarten and Seehaus; bring your own food.
Surfers riding a standing wave in the English Garden.
One of the world's largest science and technology museums.
BMW's futuristic showroom, a bowl-shaped museum of classic models and the chance to tour the Munich assembly plant.
The Wittelsbach summer palace, with a swan-filled canal, the Gallery of Beauties and a carriage museum.

items.w: Timed tickets only; snowy in winter
items.d: King Ludwig II's dream castle, the model for Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.
King Ludwig II's yellow childhood home, facing Neuschwanstein across the valley; book a combined ticket for both.
The smallest of Ludwig II's palaces and the only one he lived to see finished, with a glittering artificial Venus Grotto.
Ludwig II's unfinished copy of Versailles on an island in Lake Chiemsee, reached by boat, with an even more lavish Hall of Mirrors.
The first Nazi concentration camp, opened in 1933 near Munich. A free, sobering memorial site and museum.

items.w: Boats run year-round, reduced in winter
items.d: Electric boat past echoing cliffs to St. Bartholomä chapel.
Germany's highest peak (2,962 m), by cog railway and cable car.
Walk through a narrow gorge, dramatic when frozen.
Painted Alpine villages; Passion Play every 10 years (next 2030).
A perfectly preserved walled medieval town on the Romantic Road. Walk the covered ramparts and see the Plönlein corner.
A funny, lantern-lit evening walking tour with Rothenburg's costumed night watchman.
400 km route from Würzburg to Füssen through walled towns.
A UNESCO Baroque palace with the world's largest ceiling fresco by Tiepolo over its grand staircase.
Imperial castle, Dürer's house and the Nazi rally grounds.
Finger-sized Rostbratwurst served three in a bun, and soft, spiced Lebkuchen gingerbread.
UNESCO old town; drink smoky Rauchbier at Schlenkerla.
Medieval Danube city with the world's oldest sausage kitchen.
A lively Rhine city of Kölsch beer, Roman history and the biggest Carnival in Germany.
Gothic twin spires that took 632 years to complete. Climb 533 steps for the view, and see the Shrine of the Three Kings.
Waiters keep replacing your 0.2 L glass until you cover it.
Castles, vineyards and the Lorelei rock between Bingen and Koblenz.
Storybook castle in a forest, owned by the same family for 800 years.
Steep Riesling vineyards, half-timbered wine villages and Cochem's hilltop castle along a looping river.

items.w: Castle illuminations in June, July and Sept
items.d: Romantic castle ruin and Germany's oldest university.
Dark pine forests, cuckoo clocks, Triberg waterfalls and spa towns.
Belle Époque spa town; Friedrichsbad's Roman-Irish bath.
Chocolate sponge, whipped cream, sour cherries and a generous splash of kirsch. Eat it in a Black Forest café.
Germany's biggest lake, shared with Austria and Switzerland. Visit Mainau, a flower island, plus Meersburg and Lindau.
Port city of canals, warehouses and the Reeperbahn.
A concert hall shaped like a glass wave atop an old warehouse in Hamburg's harbour. The public Plaza with harbour views is free.
The world's largest model railway, with miniature countries, airports with planes taking off and day-night cycles.
Hamburg's Sunday fish market opens at 5 a.m. with loud traders and a live band in the old auction hall.
The Baroque "Florence on the Elbe," rebuilt after the 1945 bombing, with the Zwinger, Semperoper and Frauenkirche.
A Baroque church destroyed in the 1945 bombing and rebuilt from its rubble, consecrated in 2005.
Bach's city and the birthplace of the Peaceful Revolution of 1989, with arcades and a creative scene.
The city of Goethe and Schiller and the birthplace of the Bauhaus.
A castle above Eisenach where Martin Luther translated the New Testament into German.
A UNESCO town with more than 1,300 half-timbered houses spanning six centuries.
Narrow-gauge steam trains puffing up to the Brocken summit, the Harz's witches' mountain.
On April 30, witches and devils gather in the Harz Mountains for festivals in towns like Thale.
A national park of sandstone towers and gorges on the Elbe, with the Bastei Bridge and world-class climbing.
A Hanseatic town with the Holstentor gate, brick Gothic churches and Niederegger marzipan.
Drive or take a ring taxi around the 20.8 km "Green Hell."
Legally drive at any safe speed on derestricted sections.
Stuttgart has two world-class car museums: Mercedes' double-helix building and Porsche's floating white museum.
Volkswagen's theme park in Wolfsburg, with brand pavilions and glass towers where new cars wait for collection.
Veal sausages, sweet mustard, pretzel and wheat beer.
Roast pork knuckle with crackling, potato dumplings and sauerkraut.
Spargel season: thick white asparagus with hollandaise and ham.
Germany's signature white wine from the Mosel and Rheingau.
A warm Alpine wind makes the mountains look close enough to touch from Munich.
Bright yellow fields across Mecklenburg and Schleswig-Holstein.
The Heerstrasse in Bonn's old town becomes a pink tunnel.
A Baroque Revival cathedral on Museum Island. Climb 270 steps to the dome walkway for city views.
Berlin's grandest square, with twin cathedrals and a concert hall.
Berlin's largest palace, built for Queen Sophie Charlotte, with Baroque gardens and a Christmas market.
The 368 m Fernsehturm, built by East Germany. Ride up to the viewing deck and revolving restaurant.
An abandoned US listening station on a hill made of wartime rubble, now covered in street art.
A former concentration camp in Oranienburg, north of Berlin. A sobering half-day visit.
A former East German amusement park, abandoned for years and now being turned into a cultural park.
Libeskind's zigzag building tells 1,700 years of German Jewish history.
Contemporary art in a 19th-century railway station.
One of the world's best collections of European Old Masters, from Dürer to Rembrandt.
German history from the Middle Ages to reunification.
A museum of video game history, with dozens of playable consoles and arcade machines.
Mauerpark on Sundays, with outdoor karaoke in an amphitheatre.
One of the world's finest orchestras, playing in the tent-like Philharmonie concert hall.
A river cruise past Museum Island and the government quarter.
Dortmund's Yellow Wall or Bayern at the Allianz Arena.
Lederhosen-clad Schuhplattler dancers, yodelling and oompah bands at a Munich beer hall.
Huge thermal spas like Therme Erding, with slides, saunas and warm outdoor pools.
Germany's saunas are nude and mixed, with Aufguss rituals.
A monorail hanging from a steel frame above the river, running since 1901.
Charlemagne's capital, with his octagonal cathedral, thermal baths and Printen spice biscuits.
A fashion city on the Rhine where you drink Altbier in the old town.
Germany's oldest city, with the Roman Porta Nigra gate, baths and an amphitheatre.
A sunny university town in the Black Forest, with little water channels (Bächle) running through its streets.
A riverside student town of half-timbered houses. Ride a Stocherkahn punt on the Neckar.
An island town on Lake Constance with a lion harbour.
A castle town on Lake Constance with a medieval castle and vineyard terraces.
A pretty Bavarian town at the base of Neuschwanstein, with a monastery and a castle.
An Alpine village in the Allgäu, host of the Four Hills ski jump and ski flying.
A Franconian wine city with a Baroque residence, a fortress and its famous Old Main Bridge.
A beautiful border town used for films like The Grand Budapest Hotel.
Europe's first porcelain factory, with a hilltop castle and cathedral above the Elbe.
A medieval city with the Krämerbrücke, a bridge lined with houses and shops.
A Harz town with an imperial palace and old silver mines.
A colourful half-timbered town with a fairy-tale castle above it.
A Hanseatic city with the Town Musicians statue, a Gothic town hall and the Schnoor quarter.
A fairy-tale castle on an island in a lake, now home to a state parliament.
A Hanseatic brick-Gothic town and gateway to Rügen.
A Bavarian village with painted houses, famous for violin-making.
The village with St. Sebastian church and the classic view of the Berchtesgaden Alps.
A fairy-tale castle on a hilltop, the ancestral seat of the Prussian kings.
A small 19th-century castle perched on a cliff edge.
The only castle on the Rhine never destroyed, with medieval rooms intact.
A castle on a vineyard hill above Cochem on the Mosel.
A UNESCO-listed steelworks turned into an art and industry site.
A UNESCO-listed coal mine complex in Essen, with design museums.
A viewpoint and treetop walk over a dramatic loop of the Saar river.
A stone bridge across sandstone pinnacles high above the Elbe.
The Harz's highest peak, said to be the witches' gathering place.
Airship history; ride a Zeppelin NT over the lake.
See a Gutenberg Bible and a printing demonstration in Mainz.
Augustus the Strong's treasure chamber in Dresden.
Cars, planes and the only place you can climb into both Concorde and the Soviet Tu-144.
Munich's art museums, from Old Masters to modern design.
The "Painters' Way," a 116 km, eight-stage trail through Saxon Switzerland's sandstone towers, gorges and Elbe views that inspired Romantic painters.
The Bodensee-Radweg loops about 260 km around the lake through Germany, Austria and Switzerland, flat and lined with beer gardens and swimming spots.
A 320 km trail high on the right bank of the Rhine, past castles, vineyards and the Lorelei rock. Do a day section from Kaub or St. Goarshausen.
Germany's highest waterfalls cascading 163 m through forest in seven tiers; lit up in the evening during Advent.
The King's Chair cliff, painted by Caspar David Friedrich.
Germany's oldest national park, a wild woodland on the Czech border with a treetop walk, lynx and wolf enclosures.
Several summer evenings when castles on the Rhine are lit with red flares and fireworks while illuminated boats cruise past.
A three-day harbour festival in May with tall ships, tugboat ballet and fireworks.
Spring beer festivals with tents, rides and dirndls in Munich (Theresienwiese) and Stuttgart. A smaller, friendlier Oktoberfest.
During Lent, Munich drinks extra-strong "liquid bread" doppelbock at Paulaner's Nockherberg and other beer halls.
Germany's banking city: a skyscraper skyline next to a rebuilt old town and apple-wine taverns in Sachsenhausen.
Tart Frankfurt cider served in a stoneware jug, with green sauce made from seven herbs over eggs and potatoes.
Big Swabian pasta pockets stuffed with meat and spinach, served in broth or fried with onions.
A bread roll with pickled herring, smoked salmon or fried fish, eaten by the harbour in Hamburg.
Thuringian bratwurst grilled over charcoal and served in a bread roll with mustard.
Berlin's classic veal meatballs in a white sauce with capers, served with potatoes.
Cloudy Bavarian wheat beer with banana and clove notes, served in a tall glass.
A hilltop Benedictine monastery above Lake Ammersee with a beer garden, pork knuckle and dark doppelbock.
One of the world's oldest monastery breweries, on a bend in the Danube Gorge. Arrive by boat from Kelheim.
Sleep in a medieval castle hotel on the Rhine, like Burg Rheinfels or Schönburg, with valley views.
Berlin's grand department store, with a famous sixth-floor food hall.
Munich's daily open-air food market, with a beer garden, maypole and Bavarian stalls.
A Christmas wonderland shop in Rothenburg, open year-round, with a German Christmas Museum.
A mountaintop house built for Hitler, reached by a special bus and a brass-lined elevator inside the mountain. Now a restaurant with Alpine views.
White chalk cliffs and beech forests on Germany's largest island.

items.n: Thunderstorm over a Munich beer garden
items.d: Everyone dashes under the chestnut trees with their litre steins as the storm rolls in off the Alps.
Sun up before 5 a.m. after a night out, canal-side bars still full.

items.n: Wadden Sea mudflats at low tide
items.d: Walk across the exposed seabed of the Wadden Sea to the islands with a guide.
A chic North Sea island with dunes, beaches and thatched houses.
An island of Baltic spa resorts with white villas and long piers.
A maze of canals explored by punt, famous for pickles.
Start where the Danube rises in the Black Forest and follow Europe's most popular cycle route past monasteries and gorges toward Passau.
Turquoise alpine lakes for summer swims: Eibsee sits right under the Zugspitze, Königssee between steep cliffs.
The Black Forest's largest lake, ringed by forest, with beaches, sailing and a lakeside trail.
A dramatic gorge on the way up the Zugspitze, with walkways and tunnels cut into the rock beside roaring water.
The world's biggest sailing event each June in Kiel, with thousands of boats, tall ships and street parties.
The world's biggest heavy metal festival, turning a tiny village into a muddy metal city each August.

items.k: Rock am Ring and Rock im Park
items.d: A huge three-day rock festival at the Nürburgring racetrack each June.
An alternative, non-commercial music and arts festival on a former Soviet airbase in late June.
Berlin's Pride march in July, one of Europe's biggest, with parties across the city.
Wagner's operas performed in his own festival theatre each summer. Tickets are notoriously hard to get.
A light, sour wheat beer from Berlin, traditionally served with a shot of raspberry or woodruff syrup.
Spend a night in a Bavarian mountain hut, sharing dinner and sunrise with hikers.
Six million visitors, 14 big tents. Reserve tables months ahead or arrive at opening.
Stuttgart's three-week beer festival, a rival to Oktoberfest.
For ten days each October, Berlin's landmarks are lit with colourful projections.
Despite the name ("sausage market"), it is the world's largest wine festival, held in September in the Palatinate.
Children carry lanterns through the streets on November 11.
On autumn mornings, castles on the Rhine Gorge appear to float above a river of mist.

items.n: Golden October in the Black Forest
items.d: Beech and larch trees turning gold among the dark firs, with mist in the valleys.
Steep slate vineyards glowing at sunset in Bernkastel-Kues.
Rothenburg's citizens dress in historic costume for a weekend of re-enactments, music and fireworks in September.
Swabian egg noodles layered with melted mountain cheese and crispy fried onions. Germany's mac and cheese.
Beef marinated for days in vinegar and spices, then braised and served with red cabbage and dumplings.
In autumn, the Palatinate pairs thin, crisp tarte flambée with Federweisser, cloudy half-fermented new wine.
Zwetschgenkuchen: a sheet cake topped with rows of plums, eaten with whipped cream at afternoon coffee in late summer.
Germany's classic ski resort below the Zugspitze, home of the Kandahar World Cup downhill and the New Year's ski jump.
Germany's most famous Christmas market, opened by the Christkind on the main square, with gingerbread and finger-sized sausages.
The "fifth season": the whole city in costume for five days, peaking with Rosenmontag parades and street parties.
Germany's oldest Christmas market, dating to 1434, home of the Stollen fruit cake.
Mulled wine served at Christmas markets in souvenir mugs.
Snow drifting onto wooden stalls while you hold a mug of Glühwein and a brass band plays carols.
The fairy-tale castle above white forests; Marienbrücke may close in ice.
Frozen spray on the long pier at Heringsdorf, empty beaches and spa hotels.
A Christmas market in front of Frederick the Great's palace in Potsdam.
The Black Forest's highest mountain (1,493 m) and its biggest ski area, with gentle runs, cross-country trails and snowshoe routes 30 minutes from Freiburg.
Rent a sled and ride long natural toboggan runs down from mountain huts near Garmisch and Bad Kohlgrub.
A narrow gorge near Garmisch where in winter the waterfalls freeze into curtains of blue ice above the walkway.
One of Germany's three great carnivals, with satirical speeches and a huge Rosenmontag parade.
One of Germany's three great Rhineland carnivals, with a Rosenmontag parade.
One of the world's top film festivals each February, with public screenings you can buy tickets for.
The famous Four Hills tournament: Oberstdorf (Dec 29) and Garmisch's New Year's Day jump in front of huge crowds.
New Year's Eve street party at the Brandenburg Gate, while the whole city sets off fireworks.
Aachen's Christmas market with Printen gingerbread.
A medieval-themed Christmas market with costumed traders, jugglers and mulled mead.
One of Germany's oldest and largest Christmas markets, around the Römerberg's half-timbered houses.
A magical market in a Black Forest gorge beneath a lit railway viaduct, on Advent weekends.
Dresden's Christmas fruit bread dusted with icing sugar, made since the 1400s.
A sugarloaf soaked in rum is set alight over a bowl of mulled wine. A Christmas-market show and drink.

countries.name: Austria
countries.intro: Imperial Vienna, Mozart's Salzburg, glassy Alpine lakes, world-class skiing and coffee-house culture.

sp.text: Easter markets, apricot blossom in the Wachau (April), opera season continues, lakes start to warm.

su.text: Alpine hiking and huts, lake swimming, Salzburg Festival (late July–Aug), Danube Island Festival.

fa.text: Wine harvest and heurigen taverns, Wachau foliage, cows coming down from the pastures, Krampus runs start late Nov.

wi.text: Christmas markets, ball season (Jan–Feb), New Year's Concert, top skiing in Tyrol and Salzburgerland.

items.d: Imperial capital of palaces, opera, art and coffee houses.
Habsburg summer palace with formal gardens and the world's oldest zoo.
Winter palace with the imperial apartments and crown jewels.
Two Baroque palaces facing each other across formal gardens. The Upper Belvedere holds Klimt's golden The Kiss and the world's largest Klimt collection.
Bruegel, Vermeer and Raphael under a gorgeous dome café.
A Habsburg palace museum with Monet, Picasso and Chagall, plus Dürer's famous Young Hare and grand state rooms.
Schiele and Klimt in the MuseumsQuartier.
Vienna's Gothic heart, with a roof of 230,000 coloured glazed tiles. Climb the 343-step south tower or tour the catacombs.
One of the world's great opera houses, with performances almost nightly from September to June. Standing tickets sell for about €15 on the day.
Lipizzaner stallions perform in a Baroque hall.

items.w: Sunday Mass at the Hofburg Chapel, Sept–June
items.d: Hear the 500-year-old choir sing Sunday Mass at the Hofburg Chapel (Sept–June). Book seats ahead or queue for free standing room.
A UNESCO-listed institution: marble tables, newspapers on wooden holders and a Melange with cake. Café Central, Sperl and Hawelka are classics.
Rich chocolate cake with a layer of apricot jam and dark chocolate glaze, served with whipped cream. Taste it at Hotel Sacher or rival Demel.
A veal cutlet pounded thin, breaded and fried until it ripples, served with potato salad. Figlmüller's are bigger than the plate.
Paper-thin pastry with apples and raisins.
Vienna's biggest market, 1.5 km of stalls with spices, cheese, wine bars and restaurants, plus a Saturday flea market.
Vienna's old amusement park, with the 1897 Riesenrad wheel made famous in the film The Third Man.
Vienna is the only capital with serious vineyards within the city. Drink new wine with a cold buffet in a heuriger in Grinzing or Stammersdorf.
Mozart's Baroque birthplace under a cliff-top fortress.
One of Europe's largest medieval castles, reached by a funicular, with views over Salzburg's domes and the Alps.
Visit the film's locations: Mirabell Gardens, the gazebo at Hellbrunn and the wedding church at Mondsee.
The yellow house on Getreidegasse where Mozart was born in 1756, with his childhood violin.

items.w: Early morning before buses; snowy in winter
items.d: Lakeside village beneath mountains, plus the world's oldest salt mine.
Tyrol's capital, where a funicular takes you from the old town to ski slopes in 20 minutes. Golden Roof and Alpine views.
The Arlberg's legendary resort, with steep off-piste skiing and the wildest après-ski in the Alps.
Big resorts with high-altitude glaciers.
Europe's highest waterfalls, dropping 380 m in three stages. A path climbs beside the spray.
A UNESCO stretch of the Danube with terraced vineyards, apricot orchards, castles and wine villages.
A huge yellow Baroque abbey above the Danube with a spectacular library and church.
Art installations, a crystal cloud and gardens inside a giant's head near Innsbruck.
Styria has many hot spring resorts, including Bad Blumau, designed by Hundertwasser with golden domes and wavy roofs.
The Danube valley turns white with apricot blossom below terraced vineyards.
Fresh snow and clear skies on the Arlberg.
A Baroque church with a huge green dome. A lift takes you up to the frescoes in the cupola.
A colourful public housing block with wavy floors and trees growing from the windows, by artist Hundertwasser.
One of Europe's biggest cemeteries, with graves of Beethoven, Brahms, Schubert and Johann Strauss.
The burial vault of 150 Habsburgs, including Empress Sisi, beneath a Capuchin church.
A magnificent Baroque library hall with frescoed ceilings and 200,000 old books.
A 252 m tower with a revolving restaurant and views over Vienna and the Danube.
A grand museum with dinosaurs, meteorites and the 29,500-year-old Venus of Willendorf.
An interactive sound museum where you can conduct the Vienna Philharmonic on a virtual podium.
The only surviving Vienna apartment of Mozart, where he wrote The Marriage of Figaro.
A small museum about the classic film noir set in post-war Vienna.
Hear a concert in the gilded Golden Hall, famous for its acoustics and the New Year's Concert.
Learn the Viennese waltz at a dance school before ball season.
Eat a Käsekrainer (cheese-filled sausage) at a late-night sausage stand by the opera.
Book a private dinner in a gondola on the giant Ferris wheel.
Bad Gastein's Belle Époque hotels around a waterfall, with thermal baths and healing tunnels.
Austria's second city, with the Kunsthaus "friendly alien" museum, the Schlossberg clock tower and a UNESCO old town.
A Danube city of digital art, with the Ars Electronica Center and a lively Mariendom.
A Wachau village with a blue Baroque church tower and the castle ruin where Richard the Lionheart was held.
A lakeside town with skiing on the Kitzsteinhorn glacier and summer swimming.
Often voted Austria's prettiest village, with wooden chalets and flower boxes.
Slide down wooden miners' slides and cross an underground salt lake.
Skiing on the Kitzsteinhorn glacier from autumn to early summer.
A castle on a rocky hill reached through 14 gates.
Baroque gardens with fountains and the steps where the von Trapp children sang Do-Re-Mi.
A prince-archbishop's palace with hidden water jets that drench unsuspecting visitors.
The world's largest monastery library hall, in white and gold Baroque.
In May and June, snowmelt floods a park so that benches and trails lie under clear water.
Cycle the classic Danube route from Passau to Vienna, past Melk and the Wachau.
Shredded caramelised pancake with raisins and powdered sugar, served with plum compote.
Boiled beef with apple-horseradish sauce, root vegetables and roast potatoes. A Viennese classic, best at Plachutta.
Carinthian dumplings filled with cheese, potatoes and mint, crimped by hand.
Marzipan and pistachio chocolate balls, invented in Salzburg.
Austria's signature white wine, peppery and crisp, from the Wachau.
Austria's herbal lemonade and fruit schnapps from mountain huts.
A monastery beer hall serving beer from stone jugs.
Europe's biggest free open-air festival.
One of the world's top classical music, opera and theatre festivals, from late July through August.
Wolfgangsee, Traunsee and Mondsee for swimming.
A hand-shaped viewing platform on the Krippenstein, sticking out over a 400 m drop above Hallstatt lake.
A 48 km toll road with 36 hairpins climbing to 2,504 m, with views of Austria's highest peak and the Pasterze glacier.
The world's largest ice cave, with 42 km of passages. Guided tours by lantern through frozen halls; open May to October.
The "Eagle Walk," a 413 km trail across Tyrol in 33 stages, with mountain huts. Do a single stage as a day hike.

items.n: Alpine thunderstorm from a mountain hut
items.d: Sitting inside a hut with a Radler while lightning flashes over the peaks.
Warm evenings on a jetty at Wolfgangsee.
A town on Lake Constance, home to the floating lake stage of the Bregenz Festival.
A huge ski circus and summer bike park.
Tyrol's largest lake, nicknamed the "Tyrolean Sea," with boats and a steam railway.
A turquoise lake near Reutte, perfect for swimming and kayaking.
A shallow steppe lake on the Hungarian border, with wine, storks and windsurfing.
A deep gorge walk on wooden walkways near St. Johann.
The largest national park in the Alps, with glaciers and the Grossglockner.
A hut-to-hut trek in the Stubai Alps over a week.
The Sky Ladder, a dramatic via ferrata in the Dachstein.
Tandem paragliding over the Zillertal valley.
Apricot dumplings rolled in buttery breadcrumbs, a Wachau summer treat.
Opera on a huge floating stage on Lake Constance.
Vienna's Pride Parade in June, around the Ringstrasse.
Free open-air films and concerts with food stalls in July and August.
Formula 1 at the Red Bull Ring in Styria.
Austria's biggest rock festival, in June.
In late November and early December, men dressed as horned, fur-covered demons run through Alpine towns with bells.
Cattle decorated with flowers and bells walking down through villages.
Leaves turning in the Prater and Augarten, heurigen pouring new wine.
On autumn and winter mornings, the fortress pokes out above a sea of fog over the city.
Cloudy, partly fermented young wine sold in autumn.
A festival of digital art and technology in Linz each September.
Rathausplatz, Spittelberg and Schönbrunn.
From January to Lent, Vienna hosts about 450 balls, from the Opera Ball to the Coffee Brewers' Ball. Take a waltz lesson first.
The Vienna Philharmonic's Strauss waltz concert in the gilded Musikverein on January 1. Tickets are allocated by lottery.
One of the oldest Christmas markets in the world, around the cathedral square under the fortress.
Chic town and the world's scariest downhill.
The lakeside village under fresh snow with smoke rising from chimneys, before the buses arrive.

items.n: Ice skating at the Wiener Eistraum
items.d: Skating paths wind through the park in front of the City Hall in January and February.
Floodlit toboggan runs in Tyrol, with stops at huts for schnapps and goulash.
The most famous après-ski bar in the Alps, where skiers dance on tables in ski boots.
The world's most dangerous downhill race on the Streif in Kitzbühel each January, with a huge party.
Exclusive Arlberg ski villages, linked to St. Anton.
A sunny plateau village famous for cross-country skiing.
A lively Zillertal resort with the Harakiri, Austria's steepest groomed piste.
Cheese noodles topped with fried onions in a ski hut.
Roasted chestnuts from street vendors and hot punch at Christmas markets.
Masked processions in Salzburg in early January.
A Christmas market in front of the yellow Schönbrunn Palace.
A lakeside Advent with floating lanterns and boats.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.intro: The Alps at their most dramatic: glaciers, cogwheel railways, turquoise lakes, chocolate and cheese. Expensive, but trains and a Swiss Travel Pass make everything effortless.

sp.text: Valley blossom while resorts keep skiing into April (Zermatt and Saas-Fee into May). Many mountain lifts close for maintenance from mid-April to early June.

su.text: Prime hiking and high passes open, lake swimming in Zurich, Geneva and Lucerne, Swiss National Day fireworks (Aug 1), Montreux Jazz.

fa.text: Golden larches (mid–late Oct), cows decorated with flowers coming down from the alps, Bern's onion market (4th Monday of November).

wi.text: Skiing and sledding, Christmas markets in Basel, Montreux and Zurich, Glacier Express through snow, fondue and raclette season, Basel Fasnacht.

items.d: Car-free village beneath the Matterhorn, with chalets, glaciers and mountain restaurants.
Cogwheel train to 3,089 m with a full Matterhorn and glacier panorama.
Europe's highest cable-car station (3,883 m) with an ice palace and summer skiing.
Ski across the glacier into Italy for lunch.
Glacial valley of 72 waterfalls, the inspiration for Tolkien's Rivendell.
Ten glacier-fed waterfalls thundering inside the mountain, reached by lift.
Car-free cliff villages above Lauterbrunnen.
Railway through the Eiger to the "Top of Europe" at 3,454 m, with an ice palace and the Aletsch Glacier.
Revolving summit restaurant from On Her Majesty's Secret Service.
A lively mountain village directly beneath the 1,800 m Eiger North Face, with cable cars to First and Männlichen and trains up to the Jungfraujoch.
Adventure base between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
Tandem flight over the lakes landing in town.
Glacial-turquoise lake and lakeside villages.
UNESCO arcaded capital with bear park and Zytglogge clock tower.
Chapel Bridge, a medieval wall and lake steamers.
Boat, the world's steepest cogwheel railway and a cable car.
"Queen of the Mountains," with Europe's first mountain railway.
Lanterns at 4 a.m. and three days of piccolo and drums.
Old Town, lake baths, Bahnhofstrasse and art.
Jet d'Eau, the UN and Calvin's old town.
Exhibits at the world's largest particle-physics lab.
A medieval castle on a rock in Lake Geneva near Montreux, which inspired Lord Byron's poem. Explore its dungeons and halls.
UNESCO-listed terraced vineyards dropping to Lake Geneva. Walk or cycle between wine cellars in villages like Cully and Epesses.
The "slowest express train in the world": eight hours across 291 bridges and 91 tunnels between Zermatt and St. Moritz, in panoramic carriages.
Across the Landwasser and Brusio viaducts to Italy.
Italian-speaking Switzerland: palm trees, lakes, piazzas, grottos and risotto, with a Mediterranean feel.
The longest glacier in the Alps, 20 km of ice. See it from Eggishorn or Bettmerhorn.
A cheese-making region of painted houses. Hike to the Äscher guesthouse, built into a cliff face.
Europe's most powerful waterfall in Schaffhausen. Take a boat to the rock in the middle of the falls.
A crispy pan-fried grated potato cake, often topped with egg or cheese.
Visit the Maison Cailler factory in Broc or Lindt Home of Chocolate in Zurich for tastings.
A medieval hilltop village with a castle, a cheese dairy and the alien-themed HR Giger Museum and bar.
Warm gusts, whitecaps on the lake and impossibly clear mountains.
The peak lights up red then gold before the village wakes.
Meadows of purple crocuses as the snow retreats.
"May snow": hillsides white with wild narcissus.
A dying lion carved into a sandstone cliff, honouring Swiss Guards killed in 1792. Mark Twain called it the saddest stone in the world.
Walk along Lucerne's medieval city wall and climb four of its towers for views over the lake.
A church with five tall stained-glass windows by Marc Chagall.
Zurich's twin-towered Romanesque church. Climb the tower for views over the old town.
A hilltop square with linden trees and views over the Limmat river in Zurich.
Switzerland's tallest church tower (100 m), with views of the Alps.
The apartment where Einstein developed his theory of special relativity in 1905.
A garden with 200 varieties of roses and the classic view of the old town.
A small, clear blue lake in a forest near Kandersteg, with glass-bottom boats.
A spectacular natural rock amphitheatre in the Jura with 160 m cliffs and ibex.
A curving stone viaduct where trains enter a tunnel straight into a cliff. A classic photo spot on the Bernina line.
A UNESCO-listed Baroque library hall with 170,000 books; visitors wear felt slippers.
A medieval town on the Rhine with painted half-timbered houses.
Three medieval UNESCO castles and walls guarding a pass in Ticino.
The world's first suspension bridge between two peaks, at 3,000 m.
Switzerland's most popular museum, with trains, planes, ships and a chocolate adventure.
Switzerland's largest art museum, with Giacometti, Monet and Munch.
A modern art museum by Renzo Piano with Monet, Van Gogh and Picasso.
The International Olympic Committee's museum on Lake Geneva.
The world's largest chocolate fountain and a tasting tour.
A wave-shaped museum by Renzo Piano dedicated to Paul Klee.

items.k: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum
items.d: The story of humanitarian action, across from the UN in Geneva.
A museum of watches and enamel from five centuries.
A hilly lake city with a Gothic cathedral and lively nightlife.
A lake resort with the Freddie Mercury statue and Château de Chillon.
Chaplin's World and the fork in the lake.
An art city on the Rhine where locals float down the river in summer.
A lakeside city with Italian charm and palm trees.
A car-free glacier village surrounded by 4,000 m peaks.
A rotating cable car to Titlis, a glacier cave and a cliff walk.
A hiking hub with Oeschinensee nearby.
A car-free village above Lauterbrunnen.
Sgraffito-decorated houses in Guarda and a thermal spa in Scuol.
A stone village in a southern valley, called "the threshold of paradise."
A walled medieval town on a lake.
The classic trek or ski tour from Chamonix to Zermatt.
Rent an e-bike and ride the steep terraced vineyards of Lavaux or Valais, stopping at cellars for tastings along the way.
Watch Appenzeller cheese being made.
In Geneva or the Jura watch valley, spend a few hours with a watchmaker assembling and taking apart a mechanical movement.
Ride a Belle Époque paddle steamer on the lake.
Sliced veal in a creamy mushroom sauce, served with rösti.
Alpine macaroni with cheese, potatoes and apple sauce.
Air-dried beef from Graubünden, sliced paper-thin.
Risotto in a rustic Ticino grotto.
Hard spice biscuits from Basel.
Mini macarons from Sprüngli in Zurich.
Meringue with thick Gruyère double cream.
Rarely exported; taste Petite Arvine and Fendant.
A Swiss soft drink made from milk whey.
Zurich burns a snowman effigy to forecast summer.
Children ring cowbells to chase away winter.
Stay at a historic grand hotel, like the Bürgenstock.
Easy hike past five lakes, three reflecting the Matterhorn.
Cliff Walk, First Flyer zipline, mountain carts and the hike to Bachalpsee.
Locals jump in the river and float through the capital.
World's steepest funicular and a ridge hike.
Swim in wooden bathhouses like Frauenbad.
One of the world's biggest techno parades, with love mobiles rolling around Lake Zurich in August.
A legendary July festival on the shore of Lake Geneva, with big-name concerts and free stages along the promenade.
Jet-set ski resort with polo on frozen lake.
A valley with emerald water, stone villages and a double-arched bridge, plus the Verzasca Dam's 220 m bungee jump from GoldenEye.
On August 1, bonfires burn on mountaintops, villages hold parties and fireworks light the lakes.

items.n: Alpine thunderstorm in the Bernese Oberland
items.d: Thunder booming off the Eiger, waterfalls swelling after the rain.
On August 1, bonfires blaze on mountaintops across the country.
A stunning turquoise lake below cliffs near Kandersteg, with a gondola, hiking and summer swimming.
A turquoise lake in a forest near Flims, warm enough for summer swimming.
A 170 m suspension bridge over a glacier lake, reached by gondola and hike.
A historic Alpine pass with a cobbled road (Tremola) and a museum.
A dramatic pass road featured in Goldfinger. Walk into an ice grotto in the Rhône Glacier.
The sunniest Swiss town, with a film festival.
A pretty village on Lake Maggiore with a lakeside promenade.
A trail from Eigergletscher to Alpiglen beneath the North Face.
A long-distance route across Switzerland.
Jump, slide and abseil down a canyon.
A tandem skydive over Interlaken.
Swim at the Bains des Pâquis, which serves fondue in winter.
Hear alphorns played in the mountains.
Traditional wrestling in sawdust rings.
Regional and federal yodelling festivals bring choirs in traditional dress, alphorns and flag-throwers to Swiss towns in summer.
Ride one of Europe's steepest funiculars, at 106%.
The world's most important modern art fair.
Outdoor screenings in the Piazza Grande.
A large music festival in Nyon.
Rare wine festival; next not before 2040.
A traditional festival with stone throwing.
Stay in a Swiss Alpine Club hut.
Onion braids, confetti fights and onion tart.
Melted Gruyère and Vacherin with white wine and kirsch, eaten with bread cubes on long forks.
Half a wheel of cheese melted under a heater and scraped onto boiled potatoes, with pickles.
In September, cows wearing flower crowns and huge bells are paraded down from the summer pastures.

items.n: Sea of fog seen from above
